problem: Open-vocabulary dense 3D maps (e.g., HOV-SG, ConceptGraphs) are heavy, quickly become outdated when objects move, and fail for objects that were never mapped; LLM-based navigation works often assume instructions that already contain map knowledge.
motivation: Objects are moved frequently in real buildings, so high-detail object mapping is brittle. A map is better used as environment grounding and context that is combined with LLM semantic priors and online detection, so that moved or unmapped objects can still be found.
key_idea: Extend the text-based hierarchical osmAG map with object nodes, VLM viewpoint nodes and room descriptions, let an LLM pick candidate nodes per room from the textual map, then navigate there and verify with online open-vocabulary detection plus VLM checking.
insight: The lightweight textual map is enough for the LLM to reason about likely rooms, and online detection recovers imprecise or missing map entries (DIR up to 0.80 on unmapped objects). Ablation: removing VLM viewpoint nodes hurts most (RO O-RSR@3m 0.9 to 0.5, UO AMD 2.25 to 6.24), because queries fall outside LabelMaker's closed category set. Removing object nodes mainly degrades location precision. A small number of viewpoint nodes gives most of the gain.
method: Semantic-osmAG map: hierarchical topometric OSM-XML map (rooms as polygons, doors as passages, parent tags) enriched with textual semantic nodes; compact (3.2 MB vs 1493 MB for HOV-SG on 8 scenes)
Object nodes: LabelMaker ensemble semantic labelling of RGB-D trajectories, Mask3D instance separation, instance centroids embedded as nodes

Viewpoint nodes and room descriptions: ChatGPT-4V is asked 'What objects are in this image?' at capture locations to give open-vocabulary nodes; 'Describe the image.' per room, summarized by an LLM and attached to areas

LLM object retrieval: prompt with a simplified map (no coordinates or polygons) outputs JSON of response nodes grouped by room (max 3 nodes per room, max 3 rooms), ordered by likelihood; optional two-stage query (rooms first, then nodes of the chosen room)
Navigation: osmAG rendered to an occupancy grid (walls and doors only), A* planning, online update from depth with replanning on collisions, visits response nodes sequentially (ROS move_base)
Online detection: YOLO-World or DINO-X proposes boxes, each crop verified by a VLM (StepFun) with 'Is there a [object] here?'; the robot rotates to further views before moving to the next node

setting.backbone: ChatGPT/GPT LLM for reasoning and VLM for map building (frozen), LabelMaker + Mask3D, YOLO-World/DINO-X detector, StepFun VLM verifier
setting.observation: RGB-D camera plus pose (mapping trajectories), 2D LiDAR for localization, RGB-D online
setting.action_space: waypoint goals to map nodes executed by A* / ROS move_base (low-level velocity control)
setting.privileged: pre-built semantic map from prior RGB-D trajectories (same as baseline); base osmAG map created manually in JOSM in simulation

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks only (HM3D-SEM subset with HOV-SG-style queries, own real-world campus set); no standard nav benchmark. Real-world tables in the text use fractions (0-1) as printed; two-stage variant and ablations are in Table 4.
results: On HM3D-SEM, R-RSR is 0.66 vs 0.27 for HOV-SG on (o,r,f) queries, and average path length is 31-49% shorter. In the real world, room retrieval is 1.00 in all categories vs 0.20-0.50 for HOV-SG/ConceptGraph, and unmapped-object O-RSR@3m is 0.80 vs 0.50 for HOV-SG. The map is far smaller (0.62 MB vs 129 MB). HOV-SG is better at precise @1m retrieval on simulated data.
limitations: Small real-world evaluation (30 queries, 5 rooms, one building), with manual camera positioning and planned instead of executed paths in one room; 9 of 30 failures mainly from detector/VLM errors
Cannot search concealed spaces (drawers) and no grasping; the base osmAG map was hand-made in JOSM for the simulation, and two-stage querying loses accuracy on relocated/unmapped objects
Relies on proprietary LLM/VLM APIs and a fixed pre-built map; @1m precision below HOV-SG
